mainTopic: Sukkah 36b — Disqualified אתרוגים, the size of an אתרוג, and what may tie the לולב
overview: The amud opens by closing an earlier discussion with 'וְתוּ לָא מִידֵּי.' A ברייתא rules that an אתרוג grown in a mold into the shape of another species is פסול, and רבא adds that one still shaped like an אתרוג, even with a layered 'planks' look, is כשר. רב rules that an אתרוג pierced by mice is not הדר. The גמרא challenges him from רבי חנינא, who used a partly eaten אתרוג, and answers that חסר disqualifies only on the first day of סוכות, while mice are different because they are repulsive. A second version has רב ruling that the mouse-pierced אתרוג is הדר. The גמרא then links the walnut-versus-egg dispute over a small אתרוג to a dispute about stones on שבת, and רבי יהודה rejects רבי יוסי's proof from רבי עקיבא's huge אתרוג. A new משנה follows: רבי יהודה requires the לולב to be tied only with its own species, while רבי מאיר allows even a string. רבא explains that palm fibers and trunk count as the לולב's species, and that for רבי יהודה another species would make five species. He begins a proof from a ברייתא about סכך, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing the earlier discussion: nothing more to say
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the previous discussion about whether רבי עקיבא and רבי שמעון hold the same view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there is nothing more to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up the previous back-and-forth. It declares that the matter is settled and there is nothing more to discuss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion tried to link the opinions of רבי עקיבא and רבי שמעון. This phrase closes that line, and the conclusion is that their views do not necessarily match. After this line, the גמרא moves on to the next clause of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: And nothing more — a closing formula that ends a discussion

phrases.english: And there is nothing more.
phrases.notes: Closes the prior discussion about רבי עקיבא and רבי שמעון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion that began on the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The earlier attempt to connect the two opinions is dropped. There is nothing more to add.

steps.title: An אתרוג grown in a mold into another species' shape is invalid
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: an אתרוג grown inside a mold so that it looks like a different species is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he grew it in a mold and made it look like a different kind of creature (species), it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to quoting the ברייתא. The next case is an אתרוג that was grown inside a mold and came out looking like a different fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new case with a clear ruling: פסול. An אתרוג that looks like another species no longer looks like an אתרוג, so it cannot be used. This ruling sets up רבא's limit in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He grew it
A mold or form that the fruit grows inside of
A different species or creation
Invalid for the מצוה

phrases.english: If he grew it in a mold
and made it like a different species — it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: גִּדְּלוֹ בִּדְפוּס וַעֲשָׂאוֹ כְּמִין בְּרִיָּה אַחֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אתרוג molded into the shape of another species is פסול.

steps.title: רבא limits the ruling to a different-species shape
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ברייתא invalidates the אתרוג only if it looks like a different species. If it is molded but still looks like an אתרוג, it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They only taught this when it looks like a different species. But if it looks like its own species, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to the ברייתא. A mold alone does not make an אתרוג פסול; only the strange shape does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Growing the fruit in a mold is not what makes it פסול. What matters is whether it still looks like an אתרוג. If it does, the mold does no harm.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of — a formula that limits a ruling
Like its own natural form
Valid

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא כְּמִין בְּרִיָּה אַחֶרֶת,
phrases.english: They only taught this regarding the shape of a different species,
but if it is like its own species — it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of the ברייתא in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A molded אתרוג that still looks like an אתרוג is כשר.

steps.title: Isn't רבא's point obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: the ברייתא already says 'like a different species,' so it is obvious that a normal-looking אתרוג is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! 'Like a different species' is what we learned!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say anything. His point seems to be written right in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's own words already limit the ruling to a different-species shape. So רבא's statement seems to add nothing new. The גמרא assumes an אמורא would not state something that is already obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! — a challenge saying that a statement is unnecessary
We learned (in a teaching from the תנאים)

phrases.english: That is obvious!
'Like a different species' is what we learned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's statement in step 3 as unnecessary.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording of the ברייתא already implies רבא's point, so there was no need to say it.

steps.title: רבא is needed for an אתרוג shaped like layered planks
steps.stepSummary: רבא's point is needed for an אתרוג molded to look like stacked planks. It does not have a perfectly normal shape, yet it is still כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where it was made like planks upon planks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא is teaching about an in-between case. The אתרוג looks somewhat unusual but still basically looks like an אתרוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might have thought that any change in shape makes the אתרוג פסול. רבא teaches that layered 'planks' still count as the אתרוג's own form. Only a true change into another species makes it פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed except for — introduces a case that shows why a statement is necessary
Planks upon planks; layered sections

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
for one that was made like planks upon planks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a specific case where the statement adds new information
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any change in shape, even a layered look, might make the אתרוג פסול.
steps.terutzMaskana: A layered, plank-like shape still counts as an אתרוג's own form and is כשר.
steps.whatToRemember: A mold only makes an אתרוג פסול if it ends up looking like another species. A somewhat odd but recognizable shape, like layered planks, is כשר.

steps.title: רב: an אתרוג pierced by mice is not beautiful
steps.stepSummary: A new discussion begins: רב rules that an אתרוג pierced by mice is not הדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: An אתרוג that mice pierced — רב said: This is not beautiful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ruling of רב. An אתרוג with holes made by mice fails the requirement of הדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah calls the אתרוג 'פרי עץ הדר.' רב says damage from mice takes away that beauty. This ruling is the starting point for the challenges that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated — introduces a teaching of the אמוראים
They pierced it / made holes in it
Mice
Beautiful — the Torah's requirement for the אתרוג

phrases.english: It was stated: an etrog that mice pierced,
Rav said: This is not beautiful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the mold case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אתרוג pierced by mice is not הדר and is פסול.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי חנינא's practice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: רבי חנינא would dip his אתרוג and eat part of it, then fulfill the מצוה with what was left.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבי חנינא would dip it, eat from it, and fulfill his obligation with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב using the practice of רבי חנינא. רבי חנינא was willing to use an אתרוג that had a piece missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an אתרוג with a bitten-off piece is still good for the מצוה, then a missing piece does not ruin its beauty. So why would holes from mice make it פסול?

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? — opens a challenge
Dips (in salt or a dip, then eats some of it)
Fulfills his obligation

phrases.english: Is that so?
But Rabbi Chanina would dip it (and eat from it)
and fulfill his obligation with it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא רַבִּי חֲנִינָא מְטַבֵּיל בֵּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a pierced אתרוג is not הדר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חנינא used a partly eaten אתרוג, which shows that missing parts do not ruin it.

steps.title: But רבי חנינא contradicts the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי חנינא's practice itself seems to contradict the משנה, which rules that a חסר אתרוג is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי חנינא, the משנה is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that the challenge cuts both ways. רבי חנינא's own practice seems to clash with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says an אתרוג that is חסר is פסול. רבי חנינא used an אתרוג that was missing a piece. So his practice needs an explanation too, and this sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult
Our משנה

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Chanina, the Mishnah is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the challenge around against the source used in step 7.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules that a חסר אתרוג is פסול, but רבי חנינא used one that was missing a piece.

steps.title: רבי חנינא is fine: first day versus later days
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא does not contradict the משנה. The משנה's rule about חסר applies on the first day of סוכות, while רבי חנינא's practice was on the later days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, the משנה is not difficult for רבי חנינא: here it is the first day of יום טוב, there it is the second day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא easily solves רבי חנינא's problem. The problem of חסר only applies on the first day of סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the first day, the מצוה needs a complete אתרוג, so a missing piece makes it פסול. On the later days, completeness is not required. So רבי חנינא could use his partly eaten אתרוג then.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it works out fine for — introduces the side that has no problem, before the side that does
Here... there — a formula that resolves a conflict by splitting cases
The first day of the festival

steps.confusionAlert: 'יום טוב שני' here means the second day of סוכות and onward. It is NOT the extra day of יום טוב kept outside ארץ ישראל (יום טוב שני של גלויות).

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא מַתְנִיתִין לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Granted, for Rabbi Chanina the Mishnah is not difficult:
here (the Mishnah) refers to the first day of the Festival,
there (Rabbi Chanina) refers to the second day of the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא מַתְנִיתִין לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי חנינא in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by time (first day versus later days)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule of חסר applies all seven days, so רבי חנינא contradicts the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule of חסר applies only on the first day. רבי חנינא's practice was on the later days.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that חסר (completeness) applies only on the first day. That sets up the question of whether הדר is any different.

steps.title: But for רב the challenge remains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that רב still has a problem. The rule of הדר applies all seven days, so רבי חנינא's practice still seems to contradict רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for רב it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its first challenge against רב. The first-day answer helps רבי חנינא, but it does not help רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's ruling is based on הדר, and הדר applies on every day of סוכות. רבי חנינא used a bitten אתרוג on the later days, so it seems a damaged אתרוג is still הדר. That contradicts רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: But — here it turns to the side that still has a problem

phrases.english: But for Rav it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the challenge from step 7 after step 9 resolved רבי חנינא's side.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הדר applies all seven days. רבי חנינא used a bitten אתרוג on the later days, so a damaged אתרוג must still be הדר.

steps.title: רב: mice are different because they are repulsive
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that damage from mice is different from a human bite, because mice are disgusting. A mouse-pierced אתרוג loses its beauty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can say to you: Mice are different, because they are repulsive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by separating the two cases. A missing piece is one thing, but damage from mice is gross and ruins the beauty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every missing piece ruins הדר, which is why רבי חנינא's bitten אתרוג was fine on the later days. Holes made by mice are disgusting, and disgust is the opposite of beauty. So רב's ruling stands on every day of סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you — introduces an answer on behalf of someone
It is different
They are repulsive or disgusting

steps.whatToRemember: A חסר אתרוג is פסול only on the first day. An אתרוג pierced by mice is not הדר at all, because mice are repulsive, so it is פסול on every day.

phrases.english: Rav could say to you:
Mice are different, because they are repulsive.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב: שָׁאנֵי עַכְבָּרִים דִּמְאִיסִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between the cases (a human bite versus mouse damage)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any missing piece is the same, so if a bitten אתרוג is הדר, a mouse-pierced one should be too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Mouse damage is disgusting and destroys הדר. A human bite does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that הדר depends on how the damage looks and feels, not just on whether something is missing.

steps.title: Second version: רב rules the mouse-pierced אתרוג is beautiful
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רב rules that a mouse-pierced אתרוג is הדר, based on רבי חנינא's practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it this way: רב said, 'This is beautiful,' because רבי חנינא would dip his אתרוג, eat some of it, and still fulfill the מצוה with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a different version of what רב said. In this version, רב says a mouse-pierced אתרוג is כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רבי חנינא's practice was used to attack רב. Here it becomes רב's own proof. רב reasons that if רבי חנינא could use an אתרוג with a piece missing, a pierced אתרוג is also still הדר.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: introduces a second version of a teaching
Beautiful; the beauty requirement for an אתרוג
Dips (the אתרוג, in order to eat from it)
Fulfills his obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions! In the first version, רב said a mouse-pierced אתרוג is פסול, and רבי חנינא was a challenge to him. In this version, רב says it is כשר, and רבי חנינא is his support.

phrases.english: Some say:
Rav said: This is beautiful,
phrases.notes: Referring to an אתרוג that mice pierced

phrases.english: for Rabbi Chanina
would dip it (and eat from it), and fulfill his obligation with it.
phrases.notes: Even though part of it was missing

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב: זֶה הָדָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the discussion of רב's ruling with an opposite version, which makes the 'mice are disgusting' answer of Step 11 unnecessary.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to this version, רב holds that an אתרוג pierced by mice is still הדר and כשר.

steps.title: רבי חנינא seems to contradict the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks that רבי חנינא's practice contradicts the משנה, which says a חסר אתרוג is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי חנינא, the משנה is a problem!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source רב relied on. The משנה says an אתרוג with a missing piece is פסול, so how could רבי חנינא use one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי חנינא's practice contradicts the משנה, it cannot support רב. This is the same question that was asked in the first version. Here it is asked again because the same proof is used in the new version.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; a challenge
Missing a piece; an incomplete אתרוג

phrases.english: But for Rabbi Chanina, the Mishnah is difficult!
phrases.notes: The משנה rules that an incomplete אתרוג is unfit

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof that רב brought in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's practice, which is the basis of רב's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says a חסר אתרוג is פסול, but רבי חנינא used one that was missing a piece.

steps.title: First day versus the later days
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's rule of חסר applies on the first day of סוכות. רבי חנינא's practice was on the later days.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem. Here (the משנה) is about the first day of יום טוב. There (רבי חנינא) is about the second day and after.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no contradiction, because the two sources are talking about different days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against a חסר אתרוג applies only on the first day, when the Torah requires the אתרוג to be complete. On the later days, רבי חנינא could use a חסר אתרוג. In this version, רב holds that הדר is not ruined by a mouse piercing, so no further question is asked.

keyTerms.meaning: The first day of the festival
The second day of the festival (and the days after)
Here... there: splitting two sources into two different cases

steps.whatToRemember: In the second version, רב says a mouse-pierced אתרוג is כשר. The rule that a חסר אתרוג is פסול applies only on the first day of סוכות.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, on the first day of the festival,
there, on the second day of the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּיוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן, כָּאן בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 13 by splitting the cases by day.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case split (כאן... כאן): the two sources apply to different days
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה's rule of חסר applies all seven days, so רבי חנינא contradicts it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule of חסר applies only on the first day. On the later days, a חסר אתרוג is fine.

steps.title: The small אתרוג dispute matches the dispute about rounded stones
steps.stepSummary: רפרם בר פפא notes that the dispute over the minimum size of an אתרוג has the same measurements as a dispute about rounded stones.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'A small אתרוג...' רפרם בר פפא said: Just like the dispute here, so is the dispute about rounded stones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about the minimum size of an אתרוג. רפרם בר פפא says there is a matching dispute somewhere else, and the next step will show it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר says the minimum is the size of a walnut, and רבי יהודה says the size of an egg. רפרם is not saying the reasons are the same. He is pointing out that the same two sages use the same two sizes in another place, which helps you remember them.

keyTerms.meaning: A small אתרוג: the משנה's minimum size
A dispute
Rounded stones (used for cleaning oneself)

steps.confusionAlert: רפרם is not saying the two cases share the same reasoning. It is only a parallel in the sizes, which works as a memory aid.

phrases.english: "A small etrog," etc.
Rafram bar Pappa said:
Like the dispute here,
so is the dispute regarding rounded stones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶתְרוֹג קָטָן וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the next clause of the משנה (the minimum size).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute about the minimum size of an אתרוג (walnut versus egg) matches the dispute about the size of bathroom stones on שבת.

steps.title: The ברייתא about stones on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about walnut versus egg size for stones brought into the bathroom on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: On שבת, a person may bring three rounded stones into the bathroom. How big may they be? רבי מאיר says: the size of a walnut. רבי יהודה says: the size of an egg.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that shows the matching dispute רפרם mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally stones are מוקצה on שבת, but the חכמים allowed carrying them into the bathroom for human dignity. The two sages argue about the size using the exact same measurements as in the אתרוג dispute: walnut for רבי מאיר and egg for רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: The bathroom
A required measurement or size
Like a walnut (in size)
Like an egg (in size)

phrases.english: As it was taught: On Shabbat,
three rounded stones
may be brought into the bathroom,
phrases.notes: For cleaning; allowed despite מוקצה because of כבוד הבריות (human dignity)

phrases.english: And what is their size?
Rabbi Meir says: like a walnut;
Rabbi Yehuda says: like an egg.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the parallel that רפרם claimed in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: רפרם בר פפא's claim that the two disputes match
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about rounded stones on שבת

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's אתרוג on his shoulder
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי tries to prove that a huge אתרוג is כשר, because רבי עקיבא carried his אתרוג on his shoulder.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And for a large one, so that he can hold...' A ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי said: There was a story about רבי עקיבא, who came to the synagogue with his אתרוג on his shoulder!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the maximum size of an אתרוג. רבי יוסי, who allows a very large אתרוג, brings a story about רבי עקיבא as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה says an אתרוג is too large if one cannot hold two in one hand. רבי יוסי allows it even larger. רבי עקיבא's אתרוג was so big that he carried it on his shoulder, so רבי יוסי argues that a giant אתרוג must be כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or incident brought as proof
The synagogue
His shoulder

phrases.english: "And for a large one, so that he can hold," etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: רבי יהודה's maximum size

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yosei said:
There was an incident with Rabbi Akiva
who came to the synagogue
with his etrog on his shoulder!

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה (the maximum size).
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי's view that even a very large אתרוג is כשר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי עקיבא carrying his אתרוג on his shoulder

steps.title: רבי יהודה rejects the proof
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that the חכמים told רבי עקיבא at the time that his huge אתרוג was not הדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to him: Is there a proof from there? They also said to him then: 'This is not beautiful.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה rejects רבי יוסי's proof. The story itself shows that the חכמים objected to רבי עקיבא's אתרוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A story only proves something if everyone accepted what happened. Here the חכמים told רבי עקיבא that such a giant אתרוג is not הדר, so the story cannot show that it is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there a proof from there? (a rejection formula)
They also; even then, the חכמים objected

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה limits how large an אתרוג may be. רבי עקיבא's huge אתרוג does not prove otherwise, because the חכמים said it was not הדר.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מִשָּׁם רְאָיָה?
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said to him: Is there proof from there?
They too said to him (Rabbi Akiva):
This is not beautiful.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מִשָּׁם רְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 17.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story was not accepted at the time. The חכמים told רבי עקיבא that his אתרוג was not הדר.

steps.title: New משנה: what may be used to tie the לולב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the לולב may be tied only with its own species. רבי מאיר allows even a string or cord.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may tie the לולב only with its own species. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי מאיר says: even with a string or a cord.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: what may be used to bind the לולב together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה requires the binding to be made from one of the plants of the לולב bundle, so nothing foreign is added to the מצוה‎. רבי מאיר holds that any binding is fine, even a plain string.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: marks the start of a new משנה
Tie or bind (the bundle)
With its own species (one of the four plants)
A cord or rope

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may not bind the lulav
except with its own species,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Meir says:
Even with (a string) a cord.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין אוֹגְדִין אֶת הַלּוּלָב אֶלָּא בְּמִינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: the לולב must be tied with its own species. רבי מאיר: any binding, even a string, is allowed.

steps.title: The people of Jerusalem tied with gold rings
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר proves his view from the people of ירושלים, who tied their לולבים with gold rings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: There was a story with the people of ירושלים, who used to tie their לולבים with rings of gold.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר brings a story to prove that a לולב may be tied with something that is not its own species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gold is not one of the four species. If the people of ירושלים used gold rings to tie their לולבים, then a binding from another material must be acceptable, as רבי מאיר holds.

keyTerms.meaning: The people of Jerusalem
Rings or bands
Gold

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:
There was an incident with the people of Jerusalem
who would bind their lulavim
with rings of gold.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאַנְשֵׁי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי מאיר's opinion from Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's view that the לולב may be tied with a different material
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of the people of ירושלים, who used gold rings

steps.title: The gold rings were only decoration
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that the people of ירושלים tied the לולב with its own species underneath, and the gold rings were only for decoration.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: They used to tie it with its own species underneath (the gold rings).
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים reject רבי מאיר's proof. The real binding was made from the לולב's own species, hidden underneath the gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gold rings were not the halachic binding. They were only decoration on top of a proper binding made from the species itself. So the story does not prove that a foreign material can serve as the binding.

keyTerms.meaning: Underneath, below (the gold rings)
They said to him: the חכמים' response

steps.whatToRemember: The gold rings in ירושלים were decoration. According to the חכמים, the real binding was made from the לולב's own species, so רבי מאיר's proof is rejected.

phrases.english: They said to him:
With its own species they would bind it, underneath.
phrases.notes: The gold rings were only decorative

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: בְּמִינוֹ הָיוּ אוֹגְדִין אוֹתוֹ מִלְּמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי מאיר's proof from Step 20.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The gold rings were not the actual binding. A binding from the species itself was underneath them.

steps.title: Palm fibers and trunk count as the לולב's own species
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that, according to רבי יהודה, the לולב may be tied even with palm fibers (סיב) or with a piece of the palm trunk.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבא said: Even with the palm fibers, and even with the trunk of the date palm.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רבא explaining what counts as the לולב's 'own species' for tying. He says the fibers and trunk of the palm tree count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה said the לולב may be tied only with its own species. רבא clarifies that 'its own species' is not limited to palm leaves. Any part of the date palm, even the rough fibers or the trunk, qualifies.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
The rough fibers that grow around the trunk of a date palm
The trunk of the date palm
Even

phrases.english: Gemara: Rava said:
Even with palm fibers,
phrases.notes: One may tie the לולב with them.

phrases.english: even with the trunk of the date palm.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins and explains רבי יהודה's view from the משנה (step 19).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, palm fibers and the palm trunk count as the לולב's own species for tying.

steps.title: Why does רבי יהודה require the lulav's own species?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks what the reasoning behind רבי יהודה's view is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks why רבי יהודה insists the tie must come from the same plant. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using a string seems harmless, so רבי יהודה's strictness needs an explanation. רבא is about to supply it himself.

keyTerms.meaning: What is his reason?

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: And Rava said: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining what counts as the 'own species,' רבא asks for the reason behind the rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logic behind רבי יהודה's requirement that the לולב be tied only with its own species.

steps.title: A binding is part of the מצוה, so another species would make five
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that a לולב requires a binding. If the binding comes from another plant, there would be five species instead of four.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that a לולב requires binding, and if one brings another species, there would be five species.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question. רבי יהודה sees the tie as part of the מצוה itself, so a tie from a different plant adds a fifth species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the tie (אגד) is not just a convenience; it is required for the מצוה. Anything that is part of the מצוה counts as an extra species if it comes from a different plant. Holding five species instead of four would violate the prohibition of בל תוסיף (adding to a מצוה). A tie from the palm itself adds nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (that)
A binding or tie
A different species
Five species (one too many)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה does not object to string because it looks unattractive. His concern is that, since the tie is part of the מצוה, a different material adds a forbidden fifth species.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the material of the tie matters to רבי יהודה but not to רבי מאיר. רבי מאיר holds the לולב does not need a binding at all, so the tie is not part of the מצוה.

phrases.english: He holds: a lulav requires binding,
and if one brings another species —
it becomes five species.
phrases.notes: This would violate בל תוסיף, the ban on adding to a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The binding is a requirement of the מצוה, so a binding from a different species would make five species.

steps.title: רבא asks for the source that palm fibers and trunk are the לולב's species
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks how he knows that סיב and the palm trunk count as the same species as the לולב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: From where do I say that palm fibers and the palm trunk are the species of the לולב?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks for a source for his ruling in step 22. This question sets up the ברייתא he brings next as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think only the leafy branch counts as 'lulav,' and that the fibers and trunk are a different category. רבא wants to show from an earlier source that they belong to the same species.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this?
The species of the לולב

phrases.english: And Rava said: From where do I say it
that palm fibers and the trunk of the date palm
are the species of the lulav?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבא's ruling in step 22 and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that סיב and the palm trunk are the same species as the לולב.

steps.title: A ברייתא: what may a סוכה be covered with?
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא. רבי מאיר says a סוכה may be covered with any material. רבי יהודה says only with the four species of the לולב.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'בסוכות תשבו' (In סוכות you shall dwell) — a סוכה of any material; these are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: The סוכה is practiced only with the four species of the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins his proof by quoting a ברייתא about what may be used for סכך. רבא's actual proof point comes later in this ברייתא, on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads the פסוק broadly: any valid material may be used for the סכך. רבי יהודה limits סכך to the same four species used for the לולב. The connection to רבא's question will become clear as the ברייתא continues.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
'In סוכות you shall dwell' (ויקרא כג:מב)
A סוכה of any material
The four species: לולב, אתרוג, הדס, ערבה

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is about סוכה, not about tying the לולב. רבא brings it because it will eventually tell us something about palm fibers and trunks. Do not expect the proof to be finished here.

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'In sukkot you shall dwell,'
a sukkah of any material,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
the sukkah is not practiced except
with the four species of the lulav.
phrases.notes: These four species are used as the סכך.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the source requested in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that סיב and the palm trunk are the לולב's species.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא disputing which materials may be used for סכך.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's קל וחומר from לולב to סוכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה argues that if the לולב, which applies only by day, is limited to four species, then the סוכה, which applies by day and night, should surely be limited to four species.
steps.simpleTranslation: And logic dictates it: If the לולב, which is not practiced at night as it is by day, is practiced only with four species, then the סוכה, which is practiced at night as it is by day — is it not logical that it should be only with four species?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה supports his view with a קל וחומר. He compares the לולב to the סוכה and argues that the סוכה deserves at least the same restriction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'lighter' case is the לולב, which is used only during the day, yet it is limited to four species. The 'heavier' case is the סוכה, which is a מצוה by both day and night. רבי יהודה argues that the heavier מצוה should surely have the same restriction.

keyTerms.meaning: And logic dictates (introducing a קל וחומר)
At night as during the day
Is it not logical? (here a rhetorical question)
An a fortiori argument: if the lighter case has a rule, the heavier case surely does

phrases.english: And logic dictates:
Just as the lulav, which is not practiced
at night as it is during the day,
is practiced only with the four species,
then the sukkah, which is practiced at night as during the day —
is it not logical that it should not be
except with the four species!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהודה supports the view he stated in step 26.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that סכך must come from the four species.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the לולב (day only) to the סוכה (day and night).

steps.title: A קל וחומר that starts strict but ends lenient is invalid
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject רבי יהודה's קל וחומר, because it starts out strict but ends up lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Any logical argument that you make which begins as a stringency and ends as a leniency is not a valid argument.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים reject רבי יהודה's קל וחומר. They say an argument meant to be strict that ends up causing a leniency is not valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's argument tries to be stricter about the סוכה by limiting its materials. The חכמים point out that this strictness leads to a leniency, which the ברייתא spells out on the next amud: someone without the four species would be exempt from סוכה altogether. Because an argument cannot reverse its own purpose, the קל וחומר fails.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the חכמים) said to him
Its beginning is to be strict
And its end is to be lenient

steps.whatToRemember: A logical derivation is invalid if it starts out being strict but ends up producing a leniency.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule about how logical derivations work, not only about סוכה. It also keeps the ברייתא going toward the point רבא needs for his proof about palm fibers and trunks.

phrases.english: They said to him:
Any logical argument that you make
whose beginning is to be strict and whose end is to be lenient —
is not a valid argument.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל דִּין שֶׁאַתָּה דָּן תְּחִלָּתוֹ לְהַחְמִיר וְסוֹפוֹ לְהָקֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's קל וחומר from step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the method of רבי יהודה's קל וחומר, not the existence of the מצוה of סוכה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument begins as a stringency but leads to a leniency, so it defeats itself.
